name: The Alpine Club International
description: The world's first mountaineering club, founded in 1857. Dedicated to promoting alpine exploration and mountain culture worldwide.

name: American Alpine Club
description: America's premier climbing organization supporting access, conservation, education, and cutting-edge alpine exploration.

name: Deutscher Alpenverein (DAV)
description: The largest mountaineering organization in the world, operating over 320 alpine huts and maintaining 30,000 km of trails across the Alps.

name: Club Alpin Français (FFCAM)
description: France's national mountaineering federation promoting responsible alpine sports, training programs, and mountain hut networks.

name: New Zealand Alpine Club
description: Dedicated to climbing, mountaineering, and backcountry skiing in New Zealand's Southern Alps and beyond.

name: The Himalayan Club
description: India's oldest mountaineering institution encouraging Himalayan exploration, publishing the Himalayan Journal since 1929.

name: Swiss Alpine Club (SAC)
description: Switzerland's premier alpine association maintaining 152 mountain huts and promoting sustainable mountain sports across the Swiss Alps.

name: Japanese Alpine Club
description: Japan's leading mountaineering organization known for pioneering ascents in the Himalayas and supporting mountain research.
